name: FL-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strongly Republican district (R+14 PVI) with no incumbent on the ballot
Huge Republican fundraising advantage: Schwartzel has raised $2.1M vs. $45K for Arias
Prediction markets price the Republican at ~92%
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: This open seat sits in a heavily Republican district, and Jim Schwartzel's roughly 45-to-1 fundraising edge over Victor Arias reinforces the structural lean. Markets price the Republican near 92%, consistent with a Likely R rating rather than Safe R given the absence of an incumbent and any polling.
model.watch: Any credible general-election polling or major outside spending could shift the margin, though the district's fundamentals leave little room for an upset.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving this Southwest Florida seat to run for governor, creating an open contest in a district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. Jim Schwartzel has built a large financial advantage, raising over two million dollars, while Democrat Victor Arias has raised only about forty-five thousand and has no outside support on either side. An independent candidate trails far behind in both money and visibility.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets that put the Republican's chances above ninety percent. The open-seat dynamic adds some uncertainty, but the structural conditions strongly favor the Republican to hold the seat.
